help.title: How to play
help.index.lead: Ten short sections. Read them in order before a first game, or open the one you need.
help.s1.title: The idea
help.s1.p1: You command the body's immune cells. New infections keep breaking in until the window closes: turn {training} on Training, {normal} on Normal, {hard} on Hard. After that, destroy every pathogen still inside the body. That is the win. If an organ fails, or the body is still infected {grace} turns after the window closes, the body is lost.
help.s1.p2: Each of you commands one immune cell. Alone, every cell is nearly useless: the Monocyte cannot swallow a worm, the Killer T-Cell cannot touch a toxin, and the B-Cell's antibodies cannot reach anything hiding inside your own cells. Together, you can hold.
help.s1.p3: All seven organs count. Losing the spleen ends the game as surely as losing the heart.
help.s2.title: A turn
help.s2.p1: Every turn has three phases, and the app runs two of them for you.
help.s2.infection.name: Infection
help.s2.infection.text: Tap Draw a card. The app draws this turn's cards, places each new invader at the start of its route, and shows you what arrived, with this turn's crisis event if one fired. Then it shows the body from the outside so you can plan: what is coming, where it is heading, and how many Action Points you have.
help.s2.command.name: Command
help.s2.command.text: Your part. Tap Command your cells and spend your Action Points in any order, on any cells. Unspent points are lost at the end of the turn.
help.s2.spread.name: Spread
help.s2.spread.text: Every invader advances one step toward its target. Anything reaching an organ box attacks that organ, removing 1 integrity.
help.s2.p5: The app plays the spread out frame by frame. Tap anywhere to move it on.
help.s3.title: The board
help.s3.routes.name: The six entry routes
help.s3.routes.text: Germs enter here and march inward. Nose, Contact, Gut, Wound and Bite are five steps long. Blood is only three.
help.s3.blood.name: The bloodstream
help.s3.blood.text: The red hub at the centre. All cells start here. Every route ends here and every organ branch begins here. Any cell may Recall to the bloodstream from anywhere for 1 Action Point, losing all its forward position.
help.s3.branches.name: The seven organ branches
help.s3.branches.text: Each organ hangs off the bloodstream on a short branch of numbered circles, with the organ box itself as the final position. A germ that reaches the organ box attacks the organ.
help.s3.pips: The pips above each organ are its integrity. A damaged organ also costs you something, and the organ's own line says what: tap an organ, or its resident, and the sheet reads, for example:
help.s3.brain.name: The Brain rule
help.s3.brain.text: Inside the Brain branch, every cell moves only 1 step per Action Point, no matter how fast it normally is.
help.s3.tap: Tap any node to see what stands there and what it can do.
help.s4.title: Action Points
help.s4.p1: You get a fixed number of Action Points each turn: {training} on Training, {normal} on Normal, {hard} on Hard. A damaged Heart or Lungs costs you one each, and some crisis events add or take some for one turn.
help.s4.p2: Every action costs 1 Action Point unless stated otherwise.
help.s4.p3: Tap the AP figure, in the command bar or on the planning screen, and it lists this turn's terms and their total.
help.s5.title: Your cells
help.s5.lead: Seven cells, all starting in the bloodstream. Each has one job, and the card behind each one says why.
help.cell.macrophage.hint: Engulf: free once a turn, then 1 AP. Swallows a virus, a coated bacterium, a fungus, blood-stage malaria, or a parasite already down to its last hit point.
help.cell.macrophage.rest: Strike: 1 damage to a coated worm or parasite.
help.cell.neutrophil.hint: NET: traps every living microbe on its own space.
help.cell.neutrophil.rest: Then it is spent and returns after 4 turns, or 2 if a primed Helper T-Cell is in the bloodstream.
help.cell.bcell.hint: Never moves. Produce antibodies of one antigen class.
help.cell.bcell.rest: Coat a bacterium, worm or parasite. Neutralise a virus, or a toxin for 2 AP. Vaccinate, 5 AP in total. Search for the clone, 3 AP, for Pathogen X.
help.cell.tcell.hint: Snipe: destroys a pathogen hiding inside one of your cells. Never misses.
help.cell.tcell.rest: Range 3 on Training, 2 on Normal and Hard, +1 while a primed Helper stands with it.
help.cell.helper.hint: It kills nothing. It licenses your other cells, and only after it has been primed.
help.cell.helper.rest: Priming means an antigen has been presented, which happens the first time any of your cells engulfs or destroys a pathogen. With the B-Cell: +1 antibody per action. With the Killer T-Cell: +1 range. With the Eosinophil: +1 step. In the bloodstream: the Neutrophil returns in 2 turns.
help.cell.nk.hint: NK strike: attacks a hidden or infected cell within one step, on a die roll of 3 or more.
help.cell.nk.rest: Needs no antigen and no antibody.
help.cell.eosinophil.hint: Strike: 2 damage to a coated worm or parasite.
help.cell.eosinophil.rest: Degranulate, 2 AP: 3 damage, enough to kill a worm outright, but it burns the organ it stands in and the cell is spent for 4 turns.
help.cell.resident.name: Resident macrophages
help.cell.resident.text.hint: One lives in each organ. Patrol: 1 AP per step along its own organ branch.
help.cell.resident.text.rest: It may never leave that branch, and it must be out on the branch to meet anything: nothing can be engulfed in the organ box itself. Engulf, free once per turn: destroy one virus or coated bacterium on its space.
help.s6.title: Beating each invader
help.invader.virus.hint: Neutralise with a matching antibody, or the Monocyte engulfs it.
help.invader.virus.rest: If it hides inside a cell, only the Killer T-Cell or NK Cell can reach it.
help.invader.hidden.hint: It is inside one of your own cells, where antibodies cannot go. Killer T-Cell (never misses) or NK Cell (3 or more).
help.invader.hidden.rest: Not all are viruses: Toxoplasmosis and Chagas are protozoa that live inside cells.
help.invader.bacteria.hint: Coat it with a matching antibody, then engulf it, or trap the swarm in a NET. It divides if you ignore it.
help.invader.bacteria.rest: Up to 8 can pack into one space.
help.invader.fungus.hint: It cannot be coated. The Monocyte engulfs it directly (2 hits, so that chips it) and a NET kills it outright.
help.invader.toxin.hint: Not alive: nothing can eat it, trap it or snipe it. Antitoxin antibodies only, and neutralising costs 2 AP.
help.invader.venom.hint: Not alive, and far too fast for your B-cells. Only a ready-made antivenom dose works.
help.invader.worm.hint: Too big to swallow and immune to NETs. Coat it, then the Eosinophil strikes (2) or degranulates (3).
help.invader.worm.rest: It lodges in an organ and chews it every 3 turns.
help.invader.parasite.hint: Coat it, then strike it down: Eosinophil 2 damage, Monocyte 1.
help.invader.parasite.rest: Once it is on its last hit point the Monocyte can finally swallow it.
help.invader.malaria.hint: Three stages. Travelling in the blood: antibodies or the Monocyte. Inside liver cells: Killer T-Cell or NK Cell only. Back in the blood: antibodies again.
help.s7.title: Antibodies
help.s7.p1: An antibody only fits its own antigen class. Making the wrong one is wasted work.
help.s7.p2: Six classes: ENV and NAK for enveloped and naked viruses, EXB and ICB for bacteria outside and inside your cells, TOX for toxins, EUK for worms, protozoa and fungi. Every pathogen card names its class, and the antibody panel shows each store.
help.s7.p3: The B-Cell produces into one class at a time, up to the store's cap. Then the antibodies are spent: coat a bacterium, worm or parasite so your cells can attack it, or neutralise a virus or toxin outright.
help.s7.p4: Coating does not kill; it makes the target attackable.
help.s7.x.name: Pathogen X
help.s7.x.text: Brand new: no antibody fits. Search for the clone, 3 AP, to find the one B-cell that does, then produce it.
help.s8.title: Memory and vaccines
help.s8.p1: Once your body remembers a disease, that disease is dealt with instantly whenever it reappears: free on Training and Normal, and for 1 Action Point on Hard.
help.s8.p2: On Training, beating a pathogen is enough: your body remembers it. On Normal and Hard, only a vaccine gives memory: invest 5 Action Points across as many turns as you like against a disease you have already seen.
help.s8.p3: A remembered pathogen shows a ring on the board. Tap it to destroy it at once.
help.s9.title: Crisis events
help.s9.lead: Some cards carry a crisis. It takes effect on the turn it is drawn, and the reveal names it. Each one is a real clinical phenomenon.
help.event.immunosuppression.effect: No antibodies can be made this turn.
help.event.neutropenia.effect: The Neutrophil goes offline for 2 turns.
help.event.lymphopenia.effect: The Killer T-Cell goes offline for 2 turns.
help.event.antibodyShortage.effect: Every antibody store is capped at 2 for 3 turns.
help.event.coInfection.effect: An extra invader breaks in at once.
help.event.passiveAntibodies.effect: Every store is filled to its cap.
help.event.fever.effect: The invaders do not advance this turn, and you have 1 fewer Action Point.
help.s9.rare: A few cards carry rarer events that fire at the end of a spread, such as a malaria relapse or shingles. The log names each one and says why.
help.s10.title: Difficulty
help.s10.p1: What changes: Action Points per turn ({apT}, {apN}, {apH}), how long the infections keep coming ({wT}, {wN}, {wH} turns), how many cards a turn can bring, how many antibodies a store holds, where a worm starts, and whether surviving a disease gives memory or only a vaccine does.

about.title: About this game
about.lead: The Immunity Wars is a cooperative board game about how a real immune system fights an infection. Every mechanic in it is grounded in real biology.
about.design: Game design and concept, Kartik Chaudhary.
about.designBody: The rules, the immunology, the board, the cards, the balance of roles. Every mechanic in this game is his. He was 13 when this version was built.
about.direction: Build direction and project lead, Shantanu Chaudhary.
about.directionBody: Architecture decisions, design review, testing, and the standard that nothing ships unless the science is right.
about.codeBody: The engine, the tests and this application were written with Claude, under the direction above. Kartik designed the game. He did not write the source code, and nothing here should be read as claiming otherwise.
about.showcase: Presented at the University of Hyderabad grant showcase, August 2026.
about.privacyBody: This game collects nothing. There are no accounts, no email addresses and no tracking of any kind. Your saved game and your settings stay on this device, and nothing is ever sent anywhere.
about.licenceCode: The source code is licensed under the Apache License 2.0.
about.licenceContent: The game content, meaning the board artwork, the card designs and the rulebook, is all rights reserved.
about.classroom: If you are a teacher who wants to use this in a classroom, that is exactly what it is for. Please go ahead.
